description: Interactive guide to spaceflight physics: the rocket equation and staging, orbit speed, Hohmann transfers, the Oberth effect and a computed Δv map.
og: Design a staged rocket, size an orbit, fly a Hohmann transfer, burn at the bottom of a gravity well and read a Δv map of the Solar System computed on one stated basis: the physics of spaceflight, interactive and sourced.
brand: IMPULSE — TECHNICAL FIELD GUIDE / ТЕХНИЧЕСКИЙ СПРАВОЧНИК
llms: Spaceflight from first principles: momentum exchange, the rocket equation with a staging optimiser, vis-viva and orbit speed, Hohmann transfers and plane changes, the Oberth effect, a Δv map of the Solar System computed on one stated basis (from a 200 km orbit, impulsive Hohmann transfers, no losses), and a sourced survey of propulsion types; figures checked against NASA fact sheets and Apollo 11, Dawn, New Horizons and Parker Solar Probe flight data.

freshness.claim: As of November 2026 no nuclear thermal rocket has flown; DRACO was closed out in 2025
Dawn's 11.5 km/s described as a record for an on-board propulsion system (stated 2018; worded 'at the time')
Breakthrough Starshot: a study, put on hold in 2024 (Benford, March 2026); the initiative's own page still describes it as live
Parker Solar Probe's about 430,000 mph (24 Dec 2024) is its record speed, matched but not beaten on later passes (NASA, 10 Sep 2026; mission extended into 2029)
As of November 2026 no spacecraft has made a speeding-up burn at closest approach to Jupiter or the Sun (Juno's 2016 burn was a braking burn)
Five craft are leaving the Solar System (Pioneer 10 and 11, Voyager 1 and 2, New Horizons); four needed Jupiter, New Horizons left on launch energy alone
NEXT ion thruster status taken from a 2008 source (ground testing); a later flight is not covered
RS-25 specification sheet (452.3 s, 512,300 lb) is a manufacturer document that is reissued
